clue.text: Not entirely versatile shrub

indicators.note: not entirely says the synonym for versatile loses its final letter

parts.note: protean means versatile, able to take many forms, after the shape-shifting sea god Proteus

explanation.surface: Someone praises a plant that is adaptable, but not completely so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' cuts the last N from PROTEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The protea is a South African flowering bush, so it is a kind of shrub.

clue.text: Soft bed for contestant

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft
a bed of rock is a layer

explanation.surface: A comfortable mattress is offered to someone in a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone taking part in a game or match, so a contestant.

clue.text: Given long line to erect, am struggling

indicators.note: struggling means the letters before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone told to put up a long rope says they are having trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An octameter is a line of verse with eight metrical feet, an unusually long line.

clue.text: Cry freely, raising volume at end of tirade

indicators.note: raising means lifting the word upward, which in a down entry reads it backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large volume or book

indicators.note: end of means take the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone sobs openly, getting louder at the close of an angry rant.
explanation.walkthrough: TOME turned upward gives EMOT, then E ends tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to show feelings in an exaggerated way, letting them pour out freely.

clue.text: Was first to spot such a mysterious band

parts.note: a speck is a tiny spot
led means was first, as a runner who led the race

explanation.surface: Someone was the first to notice a strange group of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to The Speckled Band, a Sherlock Holmes mystery; the speckled band there is a snake, not a group of players.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's story The Adventure of the Speckled Band names its mysterious band with this adjective.

clue.text: Did they struggle in atelier, perhaps?

definitions.text: Did they struggle in atelier, perhaps?

parts.words: Did they struggle in atelier, perhaps?
parts.note: the question reads as painters having a hard time in the studio; it plays on a Victorian brotherhood of artists who tried to paint as if before the Renaissance master from Urbino

explanation.walkthrough: An atelier is an artist's studio. The joke is that these painters were struggling to get back before Raphael, the Renaissance painter whose style they rejected.
explanation.definitionFit: The brotherhood took its name from wishing to paint as artists did before Raphael's time.

clue.text: Tricked, and no mistake, in hearing meteorite

indicators.note: in hearing means the words are said aloud and the sound gives the answer's spelling

parts.note: conned means tricked and right is an emphatic 'and no mistake', as in 'conned, right enough'

explanation.surface: Someone was well and truly fooled by a talk about a space rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A chondrite is a stony meteorite containing small round grains, a common type that falls to Earth.

clue.text: I hád left range without compare

indicators.note: without means outside, so the pieces for left and range go around the letter

parts.note: ken is the range of one's knowledge

explanation.surface: Someone left a stove behind with nothing to match it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' is a link. 'without' means outside here, not lacking. A range is also a kitchen stove.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to compare them.

clue.text: Leading man I don't cast

indicators.note: cast means thrown or shaped anew, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A star actor says he is not chosen for the part.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominant means having the most power or influence, so it means leading.

clue.text: Bearing her absence?

parts.note: bearing reads as putting up with someone being away, but it means giving birth: time off work when a woman has a baby

explanation.definitionFit: This is time off work granted to a woman around the birth of her child, the absence that childbearing brings.

clue.text: Scientific instrument bathed city in a flickering light

indicators.note: the light bathed the city, so it surrounds the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: a strobe is a rapidly flashing lamp
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A scientific device lit a city with pulsing light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrolabe is an old device for measuring the altitude of stars, a scientific instrument of astronomers and navigators.

clue.text: One hand-picked foreign leader accepts our country in recession

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the built word is read in reverse
accepts means the leader's name takes the country inside it

parts.note: Mao Zedong, the Chinese leader
UK, the setter's country in a British paper

explanation.surface: A specially chosen overseas head of state lets Britain in during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One hand-picked' looks like part of the wordplay but is the definition; a recession is read here as a going-back, not an economic slump.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakum is loose fibre that was picked by hand from old rope, often by prisoners, so it is a hand-picked thing.

clue.text: Rudder control commonly made of wood

indicators.note: commonly means said in a common accent that drops the aitch

parts.note: the helm is the tiller or wheel that steers a ship's rudder

explanation.surface: The tiller of a boat is usually built from timber.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying the steering word with a dropped H, as in some London accents, leaves ELM; 'made of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm is a hardwood from the elm tree, so it is a kind of wood.

clue.text: Sometimes there's nobody taking turn round porch

indicators.note: round means the reversed word goes around the porch
taking a turn means the word for nobody is turned backwards

parts.note: none means nobody
a veranda is a roofed porch along a house

explanation.surface: Every so often nobody walks around the porch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking turn' gives ENON, which wraps round the porch. 'there's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The old phrase means now and again, at intervals, so it means sometimes.

clue.text: This may take the Mickey out of subject of play

definitions.text: This may take the Mickey out of
definitions.meaning: a device that catches a Mickey Mouse, removing a rodent from a house
the name of the play-within-a-play in Hamlet, and of Agatha Christie's long-running London stage show

explanation.surface: Something that mocks the theme of a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: To take the mickey is British slang for to make fun of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap for catching mice removes them, and the same name belongs to a famous play.

clue.text: Keepin' on round one bend

indicators.note: round means the clipped word for nagging goes around the number one

parts.note: harping on means keeping on, nagging; the dropped G of keepin' carries over to harpin'
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone nags, in casual speech, about a curve in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Keepin'' is the signal to drop the G from HARPING too.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairpin is a very sharp U-shaped turn in a road, so it is a bend.

clue.text: Remarkable surplus of leisure wear

indicators.note: remarkable read as re-markable means the letters can be marked out again, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: There is an amazing excess of casual clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Plus fours are baggy knee breeches, worn for golf and country walks.
explanation.definitionFit: Plus fours are loose trousers once worn for golf and shooting, sporting leisure clothes.

clue.text: In parts, poem is about one jocular lawgiver

indicators.note: is about means the word for poem goes around the following pieces

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative poem
one is the Roman numeral I
Sod is the jokey author of Sod's Law, that whatever can go wrong will

explanation.surface: A long poem, in sections, deals with a humorous legislator.
explanation.walkthrough: Sod's Law is the British name for the rule that anything that can go wrong will; Sod is its mock lawgiver.
explanation.definitionFit: Something episodic comes in separate instalments or episodes, so it comes in parts.

clue.text: Abroad, what fills role? I'm floored

indicators.note: fills means the foreign word goes inside the word for role

parts.note: a part is a role in a play
que is French for what

explanation.surface: An actor overseas, asked what part to play, says he is stunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm floored' looks like amazement but is the floor speaking: this wood is something a floor is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Parquet is wooden block flooring, so a room laid with it could say it is floored with it.

clue.text: In place of darkness finding east a puzzle

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
a rebus is a puzzle of pictures standing for words

explanation.surface: Someone in a dark spot works out an eastern riddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' and 'finding' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Erebus is the region of darkness on the way to Hades, so it is a dark place.

clue.text: One could barely finish Hamlet

parts.note: barely reads as only just, but in the soliloquy the prince says he might end his life with a bare dagger

explanation.walkthrough: In 'To be or not to be', Hamlet says he might his quietus make with a bare one of these, a small blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodkin is a short dagger, the weapon Hamlet imagines could end his own life.

clue.text: Roughly sprawled, despite wearing this on boot, up here?

indicators.note: wearing means the fall words are inside the boot gear, as if clothed by it

parts.note: a spike is a metal point fixed to a climbing boot
ca, circa, means roughly
fell means sprawled, tumbled over

explanation.surface: A walker took a heavy fall in spiked boots on top of a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'despite' is a link. The definition with a question mark leans on the whole scene: a climber high up on England's highest peak, in the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Scafell Pike is the highest mountain in England, a place where a climber is high up.

clue.text: Fit to cover miles in walk

indicators.note: to cover means the word for fit goes over the abbreviation

parts.note: able means fit, capable

explanation.surface: A healthy person can manage miles on a stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, relaxed pace.

clue.text: Starts on free range egg? Has not to

clue.text: Refuse to admit scruffy beard

indicators.note: scruffy means untidy, so the letters of the next word are messed up

explanation.surface: A club bouncer turns away a man with an unkempt beard.
explanation.definitionFit: To debar someone is to shut them out, refusing them entry.

clue.text: Terrified by a street fight involving us as subject

indicators.note: involving means taking in the pronoun among its letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'us as subject' asks for the subject form of the pronoun, not the object form. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Awestruck means filled with awe or dread, close in sense to terrified.

clue.text: More unnerving to see one strangled by ivy

one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.definitionFit: Creepier means more eerie or spine-chilling, so it means more unnerving.

clue.text: Prayer to have old leader released from confinement

indicators.note: leader released from means the first letter is let out of the word for confinement

parts.note: prison is confinement, a place of imprisonment

explanation.surface: A former head of state, freed from jail, gives thanks to God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old leader' looks like one piece, a former ruler, but 'old' gives its own letter and 'leader' is the first letter of confinement. 'to have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An orison is an old literary word for a prayer, as Hamlet uses it to Ophelia.
